The words

Jesus loves me! this I know,
For the Bible tells me so;
Little ones to Him belong;
They are weak, but He is strong.

Refrain

Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me!
The Bible tells me so.

Jesus loves me! He who died
Heaven’s gate to open wide;
He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.

Jesus loves me! loves me still,
Though I’m very weak and ill;
From His shining throne on high
Comes to watch me where I lie.

Jesus loves me! He will stay
Close beside me all the way;
If I love Him, when I die
He will take me home on high.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (B♭).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m s l — only 5 different notes, so it is a good one for a choir new to solfa. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Anna Bartlett Warner wrote the words as a poem in Say and Seal (1860), a novel she wrote with her sister Susan. William Bradbury set it to music and added the refrain 'Yes, Jesus loves me' in 1862.

The tune uses only five different solfa notes (d r m s l) and moves mostly by step, which makes it a good first song for children learning to sing from solfa.

  • Words (1860): Anna Bartlett Warner (1827–1915)
  • Refrain (1862): William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868)
  • Melody (1862): William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868)

Tune JESUS LOVES ME by William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868); words by Anna Bartlett Warner (1827–1915) and William Batchelder Bradbury (1816–1868).

Questions about Jesus Loves Me

What is the doh of Jesus Loves Me?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Jesus Loves Me start on?

It starts on s (B♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is Jesus Loves Me in the public domain?

Yes. Anna Bartlett Warner died in 1915, William Batchelder Bradbury died in 1868, William Batchelder Bradbury died in 1868; the words were first published in 1860 and the music in 1862. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
